Municipality: Henderson Township

Comments: This well was drilled in an agricultural area off of Cider Mill Road in December 2007.On 10/24/22, an NOV was issued to Stonehaven Energy when it was discovered that the brine tank had been allowed to overflow. On 3/27/23, an administrative order was issued due to a lack of remedial action from Stonehaven Energy. This order was delivered in person by Bureau of Investigations staff on 3/28/2023. As per this administrative order, a written remediation plan was to be submitted to the Department by 5/26/23, and a final remediation report is to be submitted by 12/31/23. No remediation plans have been received by the Department as of this date. A Petition to Enforce was filed in Commonwealth Court on 8/16/2023. In response to that petition, a Commonwealth Order was issued on 12/13/2023 requiring a Remediation Schedule to be submitted to the Department within 60 days. No Remediation Schedule has been received, and a new violation has been issued for failure to comply with the terms of the issued court order.During an inspection of the site on 4/20/23, it was noted that a partial soil excavation had occurred. At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any further excavation has occurred since that date. The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 12/7/2023 (Inspection Record # 3655977), there have been no changes at the site. New violations have been issued during this inspection for failure to comply with an issued court order, failure to plug the well upon abandonment, and for failure to submit annual production information.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 965087
Permit API: 053-27695
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/11/2022
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the location.Upon arriving on the location, I observed two areas of recent earth disturbance to the west/northwest of the well. The first area is in the proximity of a pipeline riser where patches of oil soaked soil remain across the excavated area. A second area located northwest of the riser (beyond the edge of the location) contains oil soaked ground and crude oil floating atop standing water in depressed areas. A third area of oil soaked ground/leaf litter was also observed approximately 100 feet into the woods to the west of the well. There are no signs of recent excavation in this area, there is no apparent surface connection between this area and the prior two.These observations indicate a recent partial cleanup of a crude oil release from the riser. Additional cleanup measures will be required throughout the area near the riser and northwest of the riser in order for those areas to be considered sufficiently remediated. As part of remediating the third area, due diligence should be given to establish the source of the product and any potential subsurface connection to the riser.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/21/2023 to PETRO ERIE INC in Sugarcreek Borough, Venango county. OGA3217(A) - PROTECTION OF FRESH GROUNDWATER AND CASING REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to control and dispose of brines produced from the drilling, alteration or operation of a well consistent with the Clean Streams Law.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/21/2023
Violation Code: OGA3217(A) - PROTECTION OF FRESH GROUNDWATER AND CASING REQUIREMENTS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to control and dispose of brines produced from the drilling, alteration or operation of a well consistent with the Clean Streams Law.
Violation ID: 8156114
Permit API: 121-44463
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2023
Comments: Onsite for a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3602052 dated 8/17/2023. The previous inspection report references a black plastic brine line, (2) brine tanks, and a separate tank battery with (4) steel tanks.There is a 100bbl fiberglass tank and a 100bbl poly tank onsite that appears to be the brine storage tanks for the well. The two tanks are plumbed together with piping and valves open to equalize the fluid in each tank. There does not appear to be a way to empty either tank by means of a water truck hose connection without altering the plumbing of the tanks. However, the 2" black poly line that runs from the hillside from the wells on the lease and ties into the brine tanks has a "T" fitting and a valve to discharge produced fluid to the ground via a ditch from a cross-culvert of the access road.The 2" valve on the black poly pipeline is closed and plugged. The pipe was not actively discharging or leaking. However, there is a visible impact area within the ditch of the cross-culvert and which the black poly line is laid. Soil conductivity readings indicate that a brine discharge has occurred at the site. The impacted area inside the ditch extends approximately 80' downslope from the access road culvert and ending just before a second culvert for another old access road. The width on average of the ditch is about 5'. The amount of the discharged produced fluid is unknown.Violations are cited.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/08/2024
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted following a reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface from 3/1/24. A workover rig is in operation drilling out plugs on the well pad following fracing operations. Equipment for the frac has mostly been removed from the location. Additional equipment was being hauled away during this inspection. I met with EQT company man Marc McCartor at the beginning of this inspection. The area of the pad surface which was impacted by the 3/1/24 release appeared dry without any visible staining. Fluid is present in the stormwater channel along the northwest pad edge. The fluid is present in the channel from the approximate halfway point of the pad edge to the compost filter sock infiltration berm at the west corner of the pad. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid is 4.46 mS/cm near the halfway point of the pad edge. Approximately 25 feet west within the channel, the EC peaked at 10.23 mS/cm and then gradually decreased as it headed farther west within the channel. The EC of the fluid where the path of the fluid ended at the compost filter sock berm at the west corner is 2.43 mS/cm. I notified the company man about the elevated EC fluid in the stormwater channel and then took sample 0718-237 from the fluid in the stormwater channel at 1242. The sample was sent to the state laboratory on the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I left a voicemail for EQT representative Rick Hall at 1338 on the same day to let him know of my findings. Later that day at 1555 I spoke with EQT representative Zac Subra. He told me that an internal investigation found that a contractor was flushing lines which had contained produced fluid following fracing operations. The contractor released what they believed to be freshwater which actually contained some portion of produced fluid. Mr. Subra said that they believe that this was the origin of the fluid in the channel and that EQT intends to pursue Act 2 remediation for this release. He also stated that a vacuum truck was already on site removing the fluid with elevated electrical conductivity. He said Penn E and R and Tobias Excavation was en route to the site to characterize and excavate the impacted material, respectively. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Violations noted against permit 081-21946.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 3/23/2026, an inspection was conducted in response to reported sloughing (IR 4163547) at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. The sloughing was reportedly discovered by the operator on 3/20/2026, on the cutslope above the access road. Range Resources representative Denny Furmanek was present at the start of this inspection. An Individual Erosion and Sedimentation permit (ESP) was issued by the Department for this site on 1/26/2024 and expires on 1/25/2029.The following was observed during the inspection:The sloughing was observed on the cutslope above the access road, as reported by the operator on 3/20/2026 (photos 3-6). This area appears to be approximately 15 feet in width and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Furmanek reported that no additional soil movement has occurred since the slough was discovered. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 2 and 7). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 15-21). The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-5). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 12). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photos 24 and 25). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 12). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the slough on the cutslope above the access road.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)Please coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESP that may be necessary for addressing the slough.

Comments: On 8/28/2026, the Department conducted a partial surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County.The inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, received on 8/25/2026.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. The area surrounding the well site is heavily saturated, with evidence of heavy animal traffic observable at the time of inspection. The gas well is equipped with a well tag. No additional equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site.- While on site, the Department spoke with Ed from Glade Pipeline Services, who confirmed that third-party disturbances are occurring at the well site due to livestock grazing, and explained that they were on site to make repairs on the access road and the well site. Based on today's inspection, a violation is being issued for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site.Additional violations will be issued in IR 4266621 for failure to implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending review of the site E and S plan in a subsequent surface inspection.The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.While on site, the Department notified Diversified representative Daniel Frick via voicemail of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations from this inspection and IR 4266621.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2022 to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 957711
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Violation ID: 8249067
Permit API: 129-24019
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Unity Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/15/2025
Comments: On September 15 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the E Shuster 2 OG Well in response to an OGI referral of the production tank leaking what appeared to be production fluid.At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled and equipped for production. The well tag was present on the well head. During the inspection, it appeared the production tank had previously been leaking and/or overflowed, but did not appear to be actively leaking. The tank appeared to be approximately 80% full at the time of the inspection.At the base of the production tank, there appeared to be an excess amount of fluid along with a thick oil based matter. There appeared to be absorbent mats on the ground next to and under the production tank where the release appeared to have occurred. Based on the amount of fluid on the ground observed by the Department, this appeared to be a reportable release (5 gallons or more). A background conductivity reading was taken and was 0.05mS. Conductivity readings were taken in the soil in the area of the spill. While some readings appeared comparable to the background reading, others were elevated in comparison to the background reading. Readings of 0.09mS 0.10mS, 0.14mS 0.31mS, 0.39mS, 0.41mS, 0.49ms, 0.64mS, 1.39mS, 1.33mS were obtained by the Department. Elevated readings were detected in about a 1 foot radius around the production tank.Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted operator representative Joe Miller to inform him of the release. Mr. Miller indicated that they had replaced/repaired a faulty dump valve the week prior. He stated field members would be at the site to assess the area for a release and remediation would occur as necessary. The Department recommended that the Operator take immediate action to remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 7 days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include:1.) An incident report including the quantity and type of fluid released (including the oil based matter) and how this was determined.2.) How long it is believed the release was occurring,3.) A timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.4.) Clarification/waste manifests for any production fluid or other production waste that has been disposed of from the site in the last 2 years.The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid (and/or other fluids) resulting in a release to the ground, as well as failure to report a release.

The last time this UIC received brine fluids was February 2024. Kendra Disposal is currently in contract negotiations with waste operators. I did a walk around site during the inspection. Please note, several areas of concern were observed during the inspection. The slope to the mechanical building has a lot of rills on the hillside resulting in erosion and sedimentation issues (photo 1). Compost sock has been installed to help collect run-off before entering into the truckers off-loading building (photo 2). The hillside has not been seeded and mulched per the E and S plans. This has been noted in multiple inspection reports since earth work started for this project over a year ago. In addition, the slope to the tank farm remains exposed. Rills are occurring on this cut-slope and sediment is collecting in the rock lined ditch. The cut-slope never had E and S blanket reapplied per the E and S plans (photos 5-7). The rock line ditch was never properly installed and/or completed after the tank farm pad was constructed. The rock line ditch just stops and doesn't connect to the sediment trap like is should according to the E and S plans (photos 8-10). Erosion is occurring along the access roads as well. Sediment is building up on the rock filters. Violations have been cited. The Department recommends addressing these issues.In addition to a site inspection at the Zelman UIC, historical background stream monitoring samples were collected at three nearby streams. Stream samples will be tested for SAC 046 plus lead and copper. These samples were sent to the Departments Lab in Harrisburg for testing. Results will be provided to the operator electronically upon receiving them.

The slope to the mechanical building has a lot of rills on the hillside resulting in erosion and sedimentation issues (photo 1). Compost sock has been installed to help collect run-off before entering into the truckers off-loading building (photo 2). The hillside has not been seeded and mulched per the E and S plans. The rock line ditch was never properly installed and/or completed after the tank farm pad was constructed. The rock line ditch just stops and doesn't connect to the sediment trap like is should according to the E and S plans (photos 8-10). Erosion is occurring along the access roads as well. Results will be provided to the operator electronically upon receiving them.

Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted a routine partial inspection at the Jobes 1 well plugging site in Georges Township, Fayette County. Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart (Next Level Energy) was on site conducting plugging operations during this inspection.The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:A Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the site entrance. However, the RCE is partially laden with sediment at the time of inspection. Additional sediment was observed in the neighboring residential yard and on Jobes Drive. The sediment observed on Jobes Drive appeared to be tracked approximately 150 feet from the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE). Significant tire rutting was observed in the neighboring residential yard and in the access road. The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan is available on site.Upon arriving to the well plugging site, the Department spoke with Next Level Energy Rig Supervisor Mike Lockhart. Lockhart cautioned the Department that high-pressure lines are active around the gas well, and suggested against approaching the plugging rig during this inspection. Therefore, the area surrounding the well plugging rig was not evaluated during this inspection due to the hazards present.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to maintain the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE), the tire rutting in the access road, the sediment tracked onto Jobes Drive, and for conducting plugging operations in a manner that causes a public nuisance.

Comments: On 06/03/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Zemba 1 well site following receipt of a spill report submitted by the operator on 05/31/2024 (CTS 381125). Penneco representatives on site. I called the operator on 06/03/2024 and they said that approximately 5 to 6 barrels were spilled on site and that the tank was cracked. The incident was discovered 05/31/2024 at 11:30 am and was reported to the Department on 05/31/2024 at 3:00 pm.Conductivity probe calibrated on 06/03/2024.The following was observed:The operator and well's information were posted on site, however the first three digits of the API were reading 126 instead of 125. I recommend that this is addressed. The tag on the well was displaying the last six digits of the API and not 125 (Photos 1, 2).Conductivity readings were taken at the site in the area that appeared to be impacted. A section of grass was dead and discolored near the tank (Photos 3-5). Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Comments: On March 3, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline, Brooke Millisock, and Clark Smith conducted a follow up site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This inspection is to follow up on a spill of 1,600 barrels of production fluid outside of containment that occurred on January 8, 2022. The southwest infiltration berm area of excavation has been uncovered and has filled with water. The water from the southwest infiltration berm area is overflowing the excavation depth and is flowing under a tarp. Due to the tarp covering the downgradient area of the excavation, the water overflowing could not be observed and could not be determined to be causing any erosion. The conductivity of the water in the in southwest excavation area was 104 uS/cm. The conductivity of the water in the southwest catch box of the well pad was 374 uS/cm. STL Resources continues to vacuum the water that has been collecting out of the catch boxes on the northwest and southwest corners of the well pad. The conductivity of the water in the northwest catch box was 7,800 uS/cm. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 8272213
Permit API: 123-47186
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

Violation ID: 8206835
Permit API: 113-20463
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/01/2024
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid from production tanks 2 and 3. It is believed that a malfunctioning ball valve somehow allowed the fluid to escape. The release was discovered around 08:00 on 10/31/24.I initially arrived onsite on 11/1/24. Mountain Energy was onsite cleaning the tanks so they could be moved to excavate the impacted area. The impacted area was already demarcated by Chesapeake. I screened for conductivity within the marked area and got readings between 0.68 to 2.30 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). Beyond the marked area, on the pad and in a rock-lined channel surrounding the pad, the conductivity readings were at or below 0.04 mS/cm. There was no fluid, staining, or other visual impacts noted outside the previously marked area.I returned to the site on 11/4/24. The tanks had been moved and the impacted area had been excavated. The excavation was approximately 30' wide by 35' long and around 10" deep. There was about 1 tri-axle load of material removed and stored on containment. Creston was in the process of collecting Act 2 confirmation samples. Creston's conductivity readings in the marked area after the excavation were at or below 0.5 mS/cm.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). Chesapeake has stated they will pursue remediation through Act 2 and the violations can be closed after that process is completed.

Comments: On August 13, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration Inspection of Diversified's Trump 8 well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following the receipt of a Well Site Restoration Report submission the Department received on 5/29/2025. Well Site Restoration Report submissions are due within 60 days of the restoration of a well site. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/12/2024, therefore shall be fully restored by 1/12/2025. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Erosion and Sediment Control Plan for the Trump 8 to be fixed to the locked gate at the access road entrance. The access road is to remain as it currently services an active oil and gas well located beyond the Trump 8. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. At the time of this inspection, the Department located the plugged well using its approximate GPS coordinate location. The Department observed the plugged well site to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this plugged well's approximate GPS location.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed erosion and sediment control features (compost filter sock - CFS ) to still be installed on site, therefore this well site is not fully restored at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the Department is denying the Well Site Restoration report submission as the well site is not fully restored. The Department recommends the Operator remove the CFS, resubmit the Well Site Restoration Report and provide the Department with photo documentation of its removal.In addition, based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued at this time for failure to fully restore the well site within 9 months of completion of plugging.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: OGA3218.2(A) - CONTAINMENT FOR UNCONVENTIONAL WELLS - SITES - Failure to design and construct unconventional well site to prevent spills to the ground surface and off well site.
Violation ID: 8263958
Permit API: 129-29235
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Penn Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/04/2026
Comments: On February 4, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Aphrodite Well Site (ESCGP issued on 5/9/2020, amended on 2/5/2024, expiring on 2/4/2029) in regards to a release reported to the Department on 2/3/2026 (CTS 394941). Present during the inspection was operator representative Jim Noon.According to Mr.Noon, this release is a seperate release, unrelated to the release documented in inspection report 4125373.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox. The access road appeared stabilized with gravel.At the time of inspection, there are 5 total wells on the well pad. According to the operator, stimulation for all 5 wells has been completed and they are continuing to install production equipment in order to get the wells into active production.During the inspection, Mr. Noon guided the Department to the location of the reported release. According to Mr. Noon the release was discovered on 2/3/2026 when containment for drilling/stimulation equipment was being removed from the site. He stated that upon removal of the containment, staining was observed and after further assessment it was identified as a release of impaired water and reported to the Department. At the time of the inspection the operator is unsure of the total volume of impaired water that was released.The Department observed the location of the spill and remediation. It appeared the area of the release and ongoing remediation was in an approximate 40-foot by 80-foot area adjacent to the well heads near the entrance of the well pad.Mr. Noon stated that 2 small temporary sumps were excavated in the area of the release in order to isolate the release. The water collected in the sumps were being pumped out by a vacuum truck. Mr. Noon stated that 2 roll-off boxes had already been filled with impacted material, and they were waiting for additional boxes to continue remediation.Conductivity readings of 18.08mS, and 6.13mS were obtained in the 2 excavated sumps. Conductivity readings of 3.97mS, 1.25mS, 1.17mS, and 0.69mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation.The Department requests the operator provide a copy of the secondary containment inspection records from January 1, 2026, through the date the secondary containment was removed, within 3 days of receiving this inspection report.The operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.If the quantity of the spill is determined to be greater than 1 barrel (42 gallons),the operator will need to perform remediation in accordance with the Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued against the Aphrodite 2M well for the observed release. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of the requested information/documentation.
